messages:
maria_ops: Heads up — after yesterday's base-image push (infra-base:nvtoolkit-2026-03-08) we're seeing container start failures on GPU nodes in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Errors look like missing libcuda/libnvidia-ml mounts. :rotating_light:
jonathan_s: Sample error from kubelet logs on a g4dn node:
```
container start failed: error mounting '/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1' to container: not found
failed to find /var/lib/nvidia/libcuda.so.1
```
samir_infra: Repro'd on a canary node. Host has driver 535.86, toolkit in image is nvidia-container-toolkit 1.14.0. Looks like the image expects `libnvidia-ml.so.1` under `/var/lib/nvidia` but kubelet/containerd mount path wasn't created by runtime.
infra-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-142 — "nvidia toolkit/base-image -> libnvidia mount failures". Affected clusters: eu-west-1-gpu-prod (subset), us-west-2-gpu-ci.
devx_liz: Are the containers using `--gpus` via docker shim or nvidia runtime? We changed to containerd + nvidia-container-toolkit in the last infra roll.
maria_ops: containerd + nvidia-container-toolkit via the OCI hooks. The problem started after bumping the toolkit in the base image; before that, nodes used toolkit from host runtime.
jonathan_s: Quick triage: this is a mount path mismatch. New toolkit packages now put libs under `/usr/local/nvidia/lib64` in our image, while the host driver exports `/var/lib/nvidia` via the runtime. The OCI hook tries to mount host `/var/lib/nvidia` into the container path and fails if the path in the container doesn't exist with correct permissions.
samir_infra: Workaround that worked on canary: create compatibility symlinks in image's Dockerfile:
```
RUN mkdir -p /var/lib/nvidia && \
    ln -s /usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libnvidia-ml.so.1 /var/lib/nvidia/libnvidia-ml.so.1
```
Then restart containerd. That made affected pods start.
oncall_kate: Do we need a node reboot for this, or just rolling pods? We have quota constraints this week, can't reprovision too many nodes.
maria_ops: No reboot necessary for the symlink fix. But we paused the base-image rollout to prevent more nodes from getting the incompatible layout.
devx_liz: Longer term options: pin toolkit package in base-image to 1.13.x which matched host layout, or migrate host runtime to provide the new path via bind-mounts. Host upgrade has risk due to driver/kernel compatibility.
jonathan_s: Also saw complaints about `libnvidia-ml` being present but `ldconfig` not picking it up in some container images. Adding `/var/lib/nvidia` to `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/nvidia.conf` helps but feels hacky.
samir_infra: Action items I propose:
- Roll back infra-base image tag to pre-toolkit-bump for remaining canaries.
- Patch image with symlink and a small `/usr/local/nvidia/README` note for now.
- Schedule host-side meeting to decide canonical layout (host vs image) and whether to always rely on host bind-mounts.
- Add unit to CI to verify presence of expected GPU lib paths after image build.
maria_ops: I've already rolled the previous tag to eu-west canary pool and paused auto-rollout. All affected pods in canary are back to green.
oncall_kate: Are any prod workloads actually OOMed or degraded? We saw autoscaler thrash earlier but that might be unrelated.
maria_ops: No observed user-facing degradation yet. We throttled new node additions, so capacity is constrained but healthy. Will keep an eye on scaling queues.
devx_liz: For the release note: "Do not bump nvidia-container-toolkit without validating container lib path compatibility with host runtime". Also add a test to kube e2e that starts a tiny GPU container and verifies `/var/lib/nvidia/libcuda.so.1` is accessible.
jonathan_s: One more gotcha: when the host driver and in-image toolkit expect different major driver ABI (e.g., 535 vs 540), you can get silent failures in CUDA init. We should add a guard that fails image build if toolkit declares an incompatible driver range.
infra-bot: INF-2026-142 updated: assigned to samir_infra; severity: medium; status: triaged.
samir_infra: I'll put up a short PR today with the symlink patch + CI check. If we get +1s, we can push a hotfix image to the remaining GPU pools.
maria_ops: Thanks, team. I'll coordinate rollback PR and notify infra-oncall before any further rollouts. :thumbsup:
